explanations.a: This is an incorrect option. Annealing softens the material by relieving internal stresses, so hardness decreases.
explanations.b: This is an incorrect option. Annealing actually improves cold workability by restoring ductility.
explanations.c: This is an incorrect option. Ductility is increased, not reduced, during annealing.
explanations.d: This is the correct option. Annealing promotes recovery, recrystallization, and grain growth, which increase ductility.

questions.question: 2. Which of the following options below shows an advantage of the heat treatment?

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option.  Reducing ductility is a disadvantage, not an advantage, of heat treatment.
explanations.b: This is an incorrect option. Heat treatment generally improves formability by relieving stresses and softening the material.
explanations.c: This is the correct option. Heat treatment can adjust hardness and microstructure to make machining easier.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option. Heat treatment typically enhances, not reduces, cold working ability.

questions.question: 3. Heat treatment is used to remove the residual stresses.

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option. Used to soften the material and refine grain structure, not primarily for removing residual stresses.
explanations.b: This is an incorrect option. Used to form spherical carbides to improve machinability, rather than to relieve residual stresses.
explanations.c: This is the correct option. Specifically performed to remove residual stresses without causing significant microstructural changes.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option. Removes effects of cold work by forming new strain-free grains, not solely intended for residual stress removal.

questions.question: 4. The hardest microstructure of steel can be produced through heat treatment.

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option. Annealing produces a soft, coarse microstructure, not the hardest one.
explanations.b: This is an incorrect option. Normalizing refines grains and increases strength but does not produce the hardest microstructure.
explanations.c: This is the correct option. Quenching forms martensite, which is the hardest microstructure in steel.
explanations.d: Incorrect, since only quenching produces the hardest microstructure.

questions.question: 5.To avoid segregation during casting and forging, which heat treatment is used?

explanations.a: This is the correct option. Homogenization annealing reduces chemical segregation formed during casting and forging by diffusion at high temperature.
explanations.b: This is an incorrect option. Normalizing refines grain structure but does not effectively eliminate segregation.
explanations.c: This is an incorrect option. Quenching locks in microstructure and does not reduce segregation.
explanations.d: Incorrect, since only annealing is used to reduce segregation.
